title: Integral and raw coherence of one operation pair
statement: Fix a prime l and an algebraic closure Ω of Q_l. Index coefficients by the finite intermediate fields E of Ω/Q_l, as in [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Let q : U → V be a morphism of noetherian schemes of finite topological Krull dimension, with l invertible on both schemes. Use the actual completed operations of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange], the ambient completed integral, raw rational and Karoubi coefficient systems of [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories], and the predicates of [def-sbc-finite-stage-rational-exchange-data]. There exist the integral comparison isomorphisms pPush and pPull and raw scalar-system morphisms rPush and rPull satisfying HasRawOperationCoherence. Thus the comparisons are exactly the scalar direct-image mate and completed pullback comparison transported by the specified ordinary/strict-tower model isomorphisms, with integral tensor-unit equations; the raw functors equal the scalar localizations of sbcPush and sbcPull, are additive, and their β are the normalized localizations of these integral comparisons. Their β satisfy the scalar tower equations and are identities at equal coefficient fields. No Karoubi extension is concluded.

proof.text: On each integral category $\mathcal B_E(W)$, [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] supplies the actual additive $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors $P_E^u,D_E^u$ and the natural transformation $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{int}}:P_E^fD_E^g\Rightarrow D_E^hP_E^e$. Its statement supplies naturality on every integral arrow, and identifies this transformation with the completed canonical mate. Thus the integral input here is defined on all derived-complete objects; neither a constructible restriction nor invertibility of the exchange is needed.

source.place: Lines 1218-1228: integral linear operations and their ambient extensions; specified integral mate

proof.text: For fixed $E$, apply the additive/semilinear part of [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to each operation, taking $R=S=\mathcal O_E$, $t=u=\varpi_E$ and the identity coefficient homomorphism. By [lem-weil-l-adic-integers-localization-uniformizer], the localized coefficient ring is $E$, so its formula is $H^{\mathrm{raw}}(v\otimes c)=H(v)\otimes c$. Apply its natural-transformation clause to $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{int}}$. The resulting component is $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{int}}(K)\otimes1$, natural for every raw arrow. Its composition clause identifies the two extended composites with $F_E^{\mathrm{raw}}$ and $G_E^{\mathrm{raw}}$.

source.place: Lines 1193-1194 and 1218-1228: central localization of integral operations and exchange

proof.text:
By [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], for each $E\subset M$ the actual tensor functors $C_{M/E,W}$ preserve ambient completeness and carry the specified natural isomorphisms $p^u,d^u$. That statement gives their compatibility with successive coefficient extensions and identities. Write $H_E:\mathcal B_E(A)\to\mathcal B_E(B)$ for either an individual operation and $b^H_{M/E}:C^B_{M/E}H_E\to H_MC^A_{M/E}$ for its specified comparison. With integral tensor associators $a^A,a^B$, this successive-extension compatibility reads
$$b^H_{P/E}(a^B_{P,M,E}H_E)=(H_Pa^A_{P,M,E})(b^H_{P/M}C^A_{M/E})(C^B_{P/M}b^H_{M/E}).$$
Use the tensor-unit maps to identify $C_{E/E}$ with the identity, as required by [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories]; the identity comparison becomes $1_{H_E}$. The tower equation remains this equation under those identifications, by substitution of the tensor-unit isomorphisms on both sides. These are the specified tensor comparisons, rather than a new choice of isomorphisms.

source.place: Lines 1297-1321: actual integral tensor, tensor-unit normalization and associators

proof.text: For $E\subset M$, integral tensor $C_{M/E,W}$ is semilinear for $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_M$: tensoring $av$ gives the same arrow as multiplication by the image of $a$ on the tensor, by the balancing relation. The image of $\varpi_E$ is nonzero in the field $M$ and hence invertible; [lem-weil-l-adic-integers-localization-uniformizer] identifies $\mathcal O_M[1/\varpi_M]$ with $M$. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to $C$, and to the composite functors at the two ends of $p^u,d^u$. This gives exactly the raw scalar transition of [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories], $v\otimes c\mapsto C(v)\otimes c$ for $c\in E\subset M$. The same lemma localizes $p^u,d^u$, their inverses, the tensor associators, the unit equations and the operation tower equations of step 3; its preservation of whiskering and composition ensures these are equations with the actual extended operations.

source.place: Lines 1300-1321: localization between different coefficient rings and normalized coherent comparisons

proof.text:
Proof: compare the two coefficient sheaf maps on every finite quotient and use
uniqueness of the inverse-limit map. Transport the direct-image scalar mate by
conjugateIsoEquiv and completed pullback by its unit-normalized strict-tower model.
Lift these comparisons and their inverses through the full complete subcategories.
Their inverse laws follow by faithfulness of the inclusions. The normalized
coefficient identity comparison, conjugated by the two model isomorphisms, gives
pPush(id); its composite with the source tensor unit is the target tensor unit.
The same argument with the completed pull comparison gives pPull(id). For three
fields, expand the two successive comparisons. Naturality moves the intervening
model maps, their inverses cancel, and the published scalar coefficient-tower
equations identify the remaining path with the single comparison through the
canonical tensor associator.
Localize the two comparisons and their inverses, conjugating by the specified
integral/raw tensor comparisons, including the equal-field tensor-unit branch.
Every raw object is integral and every arrow is a fraction of an integral arrow,
so these components determine the localized comparisons and all their equations.
The localized naturality and coefficient-tower equations give the raw system morphisms:
apply the source localization to each integral tower equation and substitute the
normalization of the raw associator. The adjacent inverse integral/raw comparisons
cancel. At E=M substitute the integral unit equations and the equal-field
normalization of the integral/raw comparison; the resulting beta components are
identities. Every raw object is Q(K), so extensionality gives HEq beta refl.
Additivity follows directly on the tensor Hom maps.

lean.statement:
theorem rationalRawOperationCoherence :
  ∃ (pPush : ∀ {E M : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω} (a : E ≤ M),
    sbcPush l (pbcFiniteField.{u} l Ω E) q ⋙
        pbcAmbientCompleteIntegralTransition l Ω V a ≅
      pbcAmbientCompleteIntegralTransition l Ω U a ⋙
        sbcPush l (pbcFiniteField.{u} l Ω M) q),
  ∃ (pPull : ∀ {E M : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω} (a : E ≤ M),
    sbcPull l (pbcFiniteField.{u} l Ω E) q ⋙
        pbcAmbientCompleteIntegralTransition l Ω U a ≅
      pbcAmbientCompleteIntegralTransition l Ω V a ⋙
        sbcPull l (pbcFiniteField.{u} l Ω M) q),
  ∃ (rPush : StageSystem.Morphism (pbcAmbientCompleteRawSystem l Ω U)
    (pbcAmbientCompleteRawSystem l Ω V)),
  ∃ (rPull : StageSystem.Morphism (pbcAmbientCompleteRawSystem l Ω V)
    (pbcAmbientCompleteRawSystem l Ω U)),
    HasRawOperationCoherence l Ω q pPush pPull rPush rPull
